safety_lead_time.comparison_action: INCREASE safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.76 days

narrative: Material PL3__M7F9E1E9 exhibits an erratic demand regime with high-volume production days (~30,000+ units) interspersed with near-zero demand days, yielding a CV of 0.58 and a gamma-like distribution. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.99, range 0.06–3.93 days), making them the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 69,300 units and safety stock of 48,301 units is recommended to achieve the 95% service level target. The current SAP zero-safety-stock configuration offers no buffer against the observed supply variability.
warnings: High demand variability detected (CV=0.58) — erratic regime requires robust safety stock
Unstable lead times detected (CV=0.99) — near-equal mean and std of lead time is the primary risk factor
Optimised policy increases total annual cost by $669.09 (+4.60%) but achieves 95% service level vs undefined baseline

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has high daily volume, near-continuous demand (96.5% non-zero days), and an EOQ well above the MOQ, making a fixed-order-quantity model with a statistically derived reorder point the natural choice. The erratic CV and unstable lead times are fully captured in the sigma_ltd safety stock formula without requiring more complex policies.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 195,673 units is not binding: safety_stock (48,301) + order_quantity (69,300) = 117,601 units, leaving 78,072 units of headroom. No capacity-driven service degradation is expected.
